# Original parser and object-rule references

Generated by `tools/generate_object_parser_fixtures.py` using Python 3.11.9
(Unicode 14.0.0) and the original `kickthemap_dxf_export.py`. The isolated
reference loader imports no application UI. Rust runs without Python.

- `parser.json`: 107 input documents, including 1,024 seeded finite binary64
  property values. Expected features come from the original parser. Covers
  group filtering, truth before trimming, missing versus null values, booleans,
  integers/floats (including integer `-0`), dictionary insertion order,
  Python string/list/dictionary representations, optional heights, Unicode
  decimal digits and float underscores, malformed geometries and polylines.
- `rules.json`: 149,112 original `ObjectLayerRule.matches` decisions. Exhaustive
  short wildcard patterns and class bodies cover Unicode, newlines, negation,
  invalid/descending ranges, escaped set operators, literal bracket gating,
  trimming, case changes and a long pattern. First-rule precedence remains
  covered by the default-rule and summary regressions.
- `python_repr_unicode.rs` in `src` freezes Python 3.11's printable character
  ranges so later Rust Unicode updates do not change property escaping.

Intentional corrections are recorded alongside the parser cases: malformed
truthy geometry containers are skipped instead of crashing the whole job;
nonfinite XY vertices are skipped and nonfinite optional Z becomes unknown.
The native parser additionally rejects oversized properties (1 MiB), more than
two million objects or ten million usable coordinates. Cancellation checks run
between feature/vertex batches; JSON decoding remains one cooperative phase.
These are operation limits, not a bound on total process memory.

Reproduce from the repository root with a Python 3.11 development environment:

    python tools/generate_object_parser_fixtures.py
    cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --test object_parser

The generator needs the development dependencies of the existing object-export
reference loader (including ezdxf 1.4.4). Fixtures are synthetic, not real project
acceptance or proof of every possible Unicode case mapping. Editable rules and
full settings/UI/export workflows remain separate migration work.
